RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the appointed candidate are women. An all-female panel selecting one woman over another provides no legal or logical basis to allege sex discrimination. Raising the gender composition of the panel would appear unfounded and could severely damage your professional credibility. 

The panel's composition is not a sign of sex bias against you. Hiring decisions for principalships often hinge on interview performance, school-specific vision, or institutional fit alongside formal qualifications. Rather than questioning the panel's gender, send a polite follow-up requesting your feedback. Frame your inquiry around professional development and learning how the committee weighed administrative experience versus classroom tenure.
